_about: How each kind of enemy fights in the rebuilt fight (rule 63b: 'Battle Brothers has its AI for the enemies correctly'; every archetype's behaviour from the library as data, before any skin). A behaviour is a set of switches the fight's one AI reads; each row quotes the wiki page (or Paolo's rule) it comes from. No number here is felt: the numbers they use (reach, hit chance, AP) are the rules' and the weapons'.

brigand_thug.quote: In the early game Brigand groups usually consist of [[Brigand Thug|Thugs]] and sometimes [[Brigand Raider|Raiders]].

lower_brigand_raider.quote: If armed with a long weapon like Pike and there are no enemies nearby, they wait to not get ahead of their melee allies.

brigand_raider.quote: If armed with a long weapon like Pike and there are no enemies nearby, they wait to not get ahead of their melee allies.

lower_brigand_marksman.quote: Their backline usually consists of [[Brigand Marksman|Marksmen]] who give Brigands ranged superiority, and if they think they have it, they will stand their ground and shoot at you.

brigand_marksman.quote: Their backline usually consists of [[Brigand Marksman|Marksmen]] who give Brigands ranged superiority, and if they think they have it, they will stand their ground and shoot at you.

brigand_poacher.quote: Their backline usually consists of [[Brigand Marksman|Marksmen]] who give Brigands ranged superiority

wiederganger.quote: They don't have any idea about careful approach and instead slowly walk towards you

direwolf.quote: Direwolves rush you even if they will have no AP left to attack.

brigand_marauder.quote: Brigand Marauders start appearing in the middle game, one or more among weaker brigands.

brigand_leader.quote: The Leader spawns in the very back and usually does not hurry to enter battle.

line.quote: However, Brigands are often too undisciplined to maintain formation. Some of them can run towards you even when they have ranged superiority.

backline.quote: if they think they have it, they will stand their ground and shoot at you

soft.quote: Being a ranged units, they can target anyone they want and prefer to shoot at shieldless units or rookies
soft.also: COMBAT [the enemy plays its part] (coordinator): 'pick the unarmoured head'
soft.how: a shot's worth is multiplied by one plus how soft the man is: no car door, a rookie (level 1), a bare head

walker.quote: slowly walk towards you, getting hit by [[Spears|spearwalls]]

rusher.source: VAMILY.md rule 63b (and bb_all/0629_Direwolf.txt: they rush you)
rusher.quote: wolves run round the back for the weakest

crew.quote: A typical battle starts with both parties in a line formation (1-2 lines deep for your forces, may be deeper for the enemy), with at least 5 hexes between parties.
crew.why: the crew keeps the line it starts in and lets the undisciplined brigands come (VAMILY rule 63b: 'the driver gate fields 12 against a crew that behaves'); it walks forward only when no foe is coming

auto._about: Rule 70b (Paolo 10/4: 'the Auto button, we are far from complete'): AUTO plays your men the way Battle Brothers' AI plays its own, formation held. Each switch the crew brain reads, with the page it comes from.

high_ground.quote: It is always advantageous to have the high ground in any battle and the AI will try to occupy the high ground whenever possible, especially their ranged units.
high_ground.how: a tile on a roof scores the rules' own height bonus per level over flat; a shooter weighs it twice

spread_attacks.quote: The AI will not stack all its attacks on the weakest target as this would be unfair and really hard to counter.
spread_attacks.how: a target's worth is divided by one plus the number of times your men already swung at him this round

keep_formation.quote: all enemies will benefit from better positioning and better coordination amongst their ranks.
keep_formation.how: a man walking toward the fight never ends more than the line's depth ahead of the middle of his own line, and prefers a tile with a friend beside him (ours.formation_depth_lines)

shield_the_backline.quote: They'll be better at protecting their vulnerable units
shield_the_backline.also: bb_all/1145_Late Game Builds.txt: 'they must not be left unprotected for highly mobile melee units will slay them without difficulty'
shield_the_backline.how: a shooter never steps level with or ahead of the front man of his own melee line while that line stands

sees_only.quote: the AI can not target anyone it can not see.
sees_only.how: a man picks only targets his side can see

raider.quote: If armed with a long weapon like Pike and there are no enemies nearby, they wait to not get ahead of their melee allies.
raider.why: a raider flanks like the line (surround: he goes for the man his friends already hold); with a two-tile weapon he never walks out ahead of the one-tile men

leader.quote: The Leader spawns in the very back and usually does not hurry to enter battle.
leader.also: bb_all/0343_Captain.txt: 'Captain is an aura that increases the Resolve of other allies by +15% (range of 5 tiles)' (ours.captain_aura)
leader.how: before the lines meet he does not move; after, he never steps ahead of his own front man, so his aura stays over his line

hunt.value: an enemy that sees nobody walks the shortest open path toward your crew, never through a house
hunt.quote: Battle Brothers has its AI for the enemies correctly
hunt.why: measured on the frozen fight (V165): enemies who never see you hold forever and the fight never ends

avoid_surround.quote: Surrounding an opponent from multiple sides makes it easier to score a hit.
avoid_surround.why: every brain weighs a tile by friends beside it against foes beside it, so nobody walks alone into three men
